claims.text: A modified Callaway model incorporating lattice distortions and point-defect scattering can accurately predict phonon thermal conductivity in high-entropy alloys.
The modified model will reduce mean absolute error by at least 12% relative to current prediction methods.
The intended material domain includes CoCrFeMnNi with varying lattice constants.
The predictive intervention is a modified Callaway model that represents lattice distortions and point-defect scattering.
Varying the lattice constant by at least 1% simulates the effects of lattice distortion on phonon thermal conductivity.
Lattice distortions and point defects affect phonon scattering.
Capturing distortion-induced phonon scattering enables accurate prediction of phonon thermal conductivity.
The model's applicability limits remain to be defined.
The model's accuracy requires validation against experimental data.
Failure of predicted phonon thermal conductivity values to agree with experimental measurements within an error margin such as 10% would falsify the hypothesis.
